_note: How each core keeps a system's save memory in its file, where that is not the memory's own bytes.
Like clocks.json, this file is NOT synced from the registry pages: the specification says what a
save's payload holds, the medium's bytes in the order the console's hardware addresses them, and
not how each core keeps them. A core absent here, or a system absent from a core's entry, keeps the
memory as it is. Layouts: expanded (fill, length: trimmed | doubled | bytes, eeprom_length),
Each entry's `evidence` says where it was read: files the cores wrote, or a MiSTer that was asked to read them.

blastem.evidence: corpus genesis/NOTES.md, 'How each core lays out the same save': five cores over thirteen games, the data identical once the layout is undone: BlastEm keeps the SRAM's own bytes at the cartridge's real size (WSB '95 32768, 8 KB carts 8192), an EEPROM as the chip, 0xFF where unwritten.

clownmdemu.evidence: corpus genesis/NOTES.md, 'How each core lays out the same save': five cores over thirteen games, the data identical once the layout is undone: clownmdemu writes 65536 bytes for every game, the SRAM on the odd lane and 0x00 on the even; it has no serial EEPROM.

genesis-plus-gx.evidence: corpus genesis/NOTES.md, 'How each core lays out the same save': five cores over thirteen games, the data identical once the layout is undone: Genesis Plus GX keeps a 64 KB image of 0x200000-0x20FFFF, the even lane 0xFF, and its libretro port reports it up to the last byte that is not 0xFF (Sonic 3 604, WSB '95 63804); an EEPROM goes through the same buffer unexpanded (Evander 128, NFL QB Club 96 253). A MiSTer did not read its WSB '95 file and did read the same bytes packed (2026-11-10).

genesis-plus-gx-wide.evidence: corpus genesis/NOTES.md, 'How each core lays out the same save': five cores over thirteen games, the data identical once the layout is undone: Genesis Plus GX Wide's files are Genesis Plus GX's, byte for byte in layout.

gba-mister.evidence: A MiSTer (GBA_20260530) showed no save for Klonoa from mGBA's 512-byte 4 Kbit EEPROM, and showed it from the same bytes padded with 0xFF to 8192 and from gpSP's 131072-byte file (2026-11-10); the core writes such an EEPROM at 8192 (corpus MISTER.md, 'What the files look like').

gpsp.evidence: corpus gba/NOTES.md, 'How each core writes the save': every gpSP save is 131072 bytes, the chip at 0, the rest 0xFF.

megadrive-mister.evidence: corpus MISTER.md, 'What the files look like': always 65536 bytes, byte-wide SRAM packed one byte per SRAM byte like BlastEm, an EEPROM at the start. A MiSTer read WSB '95 from BlastEm's 32768-byte file and from Genesis Plus GX's bytes packed, not from Genesis Plus GX's own file, and read Evander's 128-byte EEPROM (2026-11-10).

picodrive.evidence: corpus genesis/NOTES.md, 'How each core lays out the same save': five cores over thirteen games, the data identical once the layout is undone: PicoDrive writes the SRAM spread over the header's range (1024 for Sonic 3, 16384 for 8 KB carts, 65536 for WSB '95), 0x00 on the other lane, and every EEPROM as an 8192-byte file, the chip first and 0x00 after (cart.c Pico.sv.size = 0x2000).

skyemu.evidence: corpus gba/NOTES.md, 'How each core writes the save': every SkyEmu save is 131072 bytes (cart_backup[128K]), the rest 0xFF, and an EEPROM's eight-byte blocks back to front (Minish Cap 'ADLEZBGA' where mGBA has 'GBZELDA').

vba-next.evidence: corpus gba/NOTES.md, 'How each core writes the save': every VBA Next save is 139264 (0x22000) bytes, an EEPROM at 0x20000 and any other chip at 0, the rest 0xFF.
